title: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
contentObjective: I can place rational numbers, including fractions and decimals, on a number line.
languageObjective: I can explain my reasoning using the words rational number, fraction, decimal, and number line.

noticeAndWonder.context: Captain Vega zoomed in on a stretch of the treasure map between -3 and -2. A point sits about halfway between those two marks, and a second point sits a little to the right of -2. How do the positions of the two points compare, and what rational number could each one be?
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Critique the Treasure-Map Plot
revealWordProblem.text: Andrew is reading Captain Vega's treasure map. He needs to plot -3/4 on the number line. He says, "-3/4 has a 3 and a 4, so I start at -3 and count 4 more units to the left, which lands me at -7." Question: Do you agree with where Andrew plotted -3/4? Explain your reasoning and tell exactly where -3/4 belongs on the number line.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: I disagree. -3/4 means three-fourths of one unit, not -3 and then 4 more. It is 3/4 of the way from 0 toward -1, so it belongs between 0 and -1 (a little past the halfway mark). Andrew's point at -7 is far too low; -3/4 = -0.75.

launch.narrative: Captain Vega's advanced treasure map uses precise coordinates — not just whole numbers! One clue says the treasure is at -2.5 on the map (halfway between -2 and -3). Another clue points to 3/4 of the way from 0 to 1. A third clue leads to -1 1/2. To find each treasure, you must plot these exact rational numbers on the number line.

conceptIntro.heading: How do you place rational numbers on a number line?
conceptIntro.intro: A rational number is any number you can write as a fraction. This includes fractions, decimals, and integers. Many rational numbers fall between two whole numbers.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To plot a rational number, find the two whole numbers it falls between, then split the space into equal parts.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I will plot -2.5 on the number line.
First, the whole numbers it falls between: -2.5 is between -2 and -3.
The .5 means halfway, so I split the space between -2 and -3 in half.
I place my dot exactly halfway between -2 and -3. That is -2.5.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now let's plot 0.75. Which two whole numbers is it between? It is between 0 and 1.
What does 0.75 mean? It is 3/4 of the way from 0 to 1.
So we split 0 to 1 into 4 equal parts and place the dot at the 3rd mark.

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: In the explore, plot each treasure clue like -2.5, 0.75, and -1.5 at its exact spot on the number line.

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Place -3/4 and -1/4 on the trail, then decide which marker is greater.

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: -3/4 has a 3 on top and -1/4 has a 1 on top. A bigger numerator means a bigger number, so -3/4 is greater.

workedExample.label: Student answer
workedExample.work: -3/4 is plotted to the RIGHT of -1/4 and called the greater value.

optional.correctWork: For negative numbers, a bigger numerator does NOT mean a bigger value. -3/4 = -0.75 and -1/4 = -0.25. On the number line, -3/4 is farther LEFT than -1/4, so -3/4 is actually LESS than -1/4. The marker -3/4 should be plotted to the left of -1/4, and -1/4 is the greater value.
hints: Turn each fraction into a decimal: what is -3/4 and what is -1/4?
On a number line, the value farther to the left is always less, even when the numerator looks bigger.

approaching.title: Spot the Mistake: Plotting 1.5

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: 1.5 has a 1 and a 5, so I will plot it between 1 and 5.

workedExample.label: Student answer
workedExample.work: Point plotted at about 3, halfway between 1 and 5.

approaching.correctWork: 1.5 does NOT mean between 1 and 5. The .5 is one half, so 1.5 is halfway between 1 and 2. I find the two whole numbers it falls between (1 and 2), split that space in half, and place the dot at the middle. The point belongs at 1.5, not 3.
hints: What does the .5 in 1.5 mean — is it a separate whole number or a part of one?
Which two whole numbers is 1.5 between? Split that space into equal parts.

onLevel.label: Plot these rational numbers: -3.5, -1/4, 2.75, -2, 1 1/2

onLevel.stem: Which rational number is closest to 0 on the number line?
onLevel.explanation: |-1/4| = 0.25, |0.5| = 0.5, |-2| = 2, |1.75| = 1.75. Since 0.25 is the smallest absolute value, -1/4 is closest to zero.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.

onLevel.title: Spot the Mistake: Plotting -2.25

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: It is negative, so I go past -2. The .25 is one quarter, so I count toward 0 (to the right) by a quarter unit and land between -2 and -1.

onLevel.correctWork: Going more negative means moving LEFT, not right. -2.25 is between -2 and -3 (it is a quarter of a unit to the LEFT of -2), not between -2 and -1. I split the space from -2 to -3 into 4 equal parts and place the dot at the first mark past -2, at -2.25.
hints: On a number line, which direction is 'more negative' — left or right?
Which two whole numbers is -2.25 between? It is just past -2 heading toward -3.

onLevel.stem: Which number is farthest to the LEFT on a number line?
onLevel.explanation: Farther left means more negative: -4 < -1 < 0 < 2, so -4 is farthest left.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.

onLevel.explanation: The opposite of a number is its reflection across 0, so the opposite of -3/4 is 3/4.
choiceFeedback: Double-check: verify the math step-by-step against the question.

extending.title: Find the Plotting Error

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: -3/4 has a 3 and a 4, so I go to -3 on the number line and then count 4 more to the left

extending.correctWork: -3/4 means negative three-fourths, which is 3/4 of the way from 0 toward -1. It should be plotted between 0 and -1, not at -7. The student treated the numerator and denominator as separate whole numbers.
hints: What does the fraction 3/4 actually mean? How much of a whole is it?
-3/4 is a number between 0 and -1. It is 3/4 of one unit to the left of zero.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Rational Numbers on the Number Line is treating the numerator and denominator of a negative fraction as two separate whole numbers instead of one value between two integers — for example, plotting -3/4 by going to -3 and then counting 4 more units to the left, landing (incorrectly) at -7, instead of recognizing that -3/4 = -0.75, which sits between 0 and -1. Before you submit an answer, find the two whole numbers your value falls between, then split that space into equal parts.

diagram.title: Lake Water Levels vs. Normal
diagram.caption: 0 is the normal level; each dot shows that day's reading, so decimals like -1.25 land between -1 and -2, more precise than whole feet.

connect.scenario: A scientist measures the water level of a lake relative to normal level (0). Monday: +0.75 ft, Tuesday: -1.25 ft, Wednesday: -0.5 ft, Thursday: +1.5 ft. She needs to plot these on a graph to track changes.
connect.promptQuestion: How do rational numbers help the scientist describe water levels more precisely than integers alone?
connect.prompt: Rational numbers help because ___. For example, -1.25 ft means the water is ___ below normal, which is between ___ and ___ on the number line. Without fractions and decimals, the scientist could only say ___.

exitTicket.stem: Which rational number is located between -2 and -3 on the number line?
exitTicket.explanation: -2.75 is between -2 and -3 because it is 0.75 units to the left of -2. -1.5 is between -1 and -2, and -3.5 is between -3 and -4.
choiceFeedback: -1.5 is to the right of -2, not between -2 and -3.
-3.5 is past -3 — you need a value between -2 and -3.
2.5 is positive — look on the negative side.
